intended_object: A closed additive subgroup H of a topological ℤ_p-module M, seen as a closed ℤ_p-submodule with the same carrier. This is the map behind the correspondence between closed subgroups and closed submodules, as stated in the docstring and in the module documentation (`closedAddSubgroupPadicIntSubmoduleOrderIso`).
explanation:
The definition keeps the carrier and the additive-subgroup structure of H. It gets closure under ℤ_p-scalars from `ClosedAddSubgroup.padicInt_smul_mem`, and that lemma is correct: the natural numbers are dense in ℤ_p, H is closed, and c ↦ c • x is continuous. Closedness is carried over unchanged. Proof terms do not matter for a structure built this way. Together with the simp lemmas `coe_toPadicIntSubmodule` and `mem_toPadicIntSubmodule`, this is exactly the intended object. It uses only the needed hypotheses: an additive group with a topology, a ℤ_p-module structure and continuous scalar multiplication. No Hausdorff or compactness assumption is made.

The ℤ_p setting is part of the content, because the argument relies on ℕ being dense in ℤ_p. It is the p-adic analogue of Mathlib's ℝ-specific automatic-linearity results. A version for any topological ring in which ℕ is dense would not be a standard notion, so the definition is not too narrow. I found no Mathlib declaration that turns a closed subgroup into a closed ℤ_p-submodule.
